symptom: In a disposable Linux synthetic probe, O_CLOEXEC prevented an otherwise permissive exec from inheriting a directory descriptor, while explicit pass_fds intentionally granted the same live object. SCM_RIGHTS conveyed a live directory FD to a receiver, which read exact synthetic bytes after the sender closed its copy. These are process capability-lifetime semantics, not authenticated provenance or production readiness.
lesson: O_CLOEXEC is a default exec inheritance boundary, not a ban on deliberate descriptor grants. Explicit pass_fds can expose the descriptor to an exec child, and SCM_RIGHTS transfers a live kernel directory reference even when the sender closes its own FD. Neither the receiver's fstat match nor successful FD-relative read authenticates the sender, initial directory provenance, namespace reachability or durable storage.
guardrail: Treat directory FDs as owned capabilities across process boundaries. Preserve O_CLOEXEC by default, require explicit authorized grants, validate ancillary-message count/truncation and peer authorization, bind a separately authenticated directory identity to the handoff, and fail closed on transfer or lifetime errors. Reuse prior closed-FD reuse and Python-source escaping guardrails. Do not introduce production native bridging, Current BUY/LINE/public/automated betting, protected N2 activation or automatic recovery.
